outcome: risk factors (placenta previa, previous LSCS, multiparity)
maternal complications (bladder injury, intraoperative blood loss, blood transfusion, caesarean hysterectomy)
fetal outcomes (pre-term delivery, low birth weight, NICU admission)
cohort: The study included 45 patients diagnosed with Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) presenting to various departments (Antenatal Outpatient Department, Emergency Labour Room, High-Risk Pregnancy Room, Intensive care unit) of a tertiary care hospital.
finding: The study found that Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) cases in a tertiary care setting were associated with significant maternal complications, including intraoperative blood loss (>1.5L in 55.6%) and caesarean hysterectomy (33.3%), as well as high rates of fetal complications such as pre-term delivery (66.7%) and low birth weight (53.3%).
